Let $B = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]$ and $A$ be a $2 \times 2$ matrix satisfying \left(A^{T}\right)- 1 = A .$

If $X = ABA^{T},$~then $A^{T}X^{2021}A =$

$
questions.solution:
Given& \left(A^{T}\right)- 1 = A, ⇒ AA^{T} = A^{T}A = I .$

Now,~$X = ABA^{T}$

$⇒ X^{2021} = \left($ABA^{T}\right)2021$

$⇒ X^{2021} = \left($ABA^{T}\right)\left($ABA^{T}\$right)\left($ABA^{T}\right) . . . \left(ABA^{T}\right)$

We know that, the matrix multiplication is associative i.e. for three matrices, we have~\left(PQ\right)R = P\left(QR\right) .$

$⇒ X^{2021} = AB\left(A^{T}A\$right)B\left($A^{T}A\right)B\left(A^{T}A\right) . . . \left(A^{T}A\right)BA^{T}$

Using the given condition, we get

$⇒ X^{2021} = AB\left(I\$right)B\left($I\right)B\left(I\right) . . . \left(I\right)BA^{T}$

$⇒ X^{2021} = ABBB . . . BA^{T}$

$⇒ X^{2021} = AB^{2021}A^{T}$

$⇒ A^{T}X^{2021}A = A^{T}AB^{2021}A^{T}A$

$⇒ A^{T}X^{2021}A = IB^{2021}I = B^{2021} .$

Now~$B^{2} = BB = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\$right]\left[\begin{cases}$1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}$1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}$1 \text{ and } 2 $\times$2 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right] .$

And~$B^{3} = B^{2}B = \left[\begin{cases}$1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right]\left[\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 2 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right] = \$left[\begin{cases}$1 \text{ and } 6 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}1 \text{ and } 2 \times3 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right] .$

And~$B^{4} = B^{3}B = \$left[\begin{cases}$1 \text{ and } 6 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\$right]\left[\begin{cases}$1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = $\$left[\begin{cases}1 & 8 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}$1 \text{ and } 2 $\times$4 \\ 0 \text{ and } 1\end{cases}\right] .$

Hence,~$B^{2021} = = $\$left[\begin{cases}1 & 2 $\times$2021 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] = \left[\begin{cases}$1 & 4042 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] .$

Hence,~$A^{T}X^{2021}A = $\$left[\begin{cases}1 & 4042 \\ 0 & 1\end{cases}\right] .$

$

questions.q: If $A$ is a non-zero square matrix of order $n$ with $\operatorname{det}(I+A) \neq 0$ and $A^3=O$, where $I, O$ are unit and null matrices of order $n \times n$ respectively, then $(I+A)^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $|I+A| \neq O$
ie, $(A+I)$ is a non-singular matrix.
$O \rightarrow$ Null Matrix
$I \rightarrow$ Unit Matrix
$\because \quad I^3=I\Rightarrow \quad A^3=0\Rightarrow \quad A^3+I=O+I\Rightarrow \quad A^3+I^3=O+I\Rightarrow \quad(A+I)\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(O+I)(A+I)\left(A^2-A+I\right)=I \quad \because(O+I=I)$
Operate $(A+I)^{-1}$ on both sides
\left\{(A+I)^{-1}(A+I)\right\}\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(A+I)^{-1} \cdot I\Rightarrow \quad I \cdot\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(A+I)^{-1}  \left(\becauseI \cdot(A+I)^{-1}=(A+I)^{-1}\right)\Rightarrow \$quad(A+I)^{-1}=\left($A^2-A+I\right)$
or
$(I+A)^{-1}=  \left($I-A+A²\right)

$⇒ Det \left(PM\right) = = Det {\left(A - I\right)}^{2} \times Det \left(P\right)$

$⇒ DetM = = {\left(Det\left(A - I\right)\right)}^{2}$

Now $A - I = \left[\begin{cases}1 & 7 & {w}^{2} \\ - 1 & - w - 1 & 1 \\ 0 & - w & - w\end{cases}\right]$

$Det \left(A - I\right) = \left({w}^{2} + w + w\right) + 7\left(- w\right) + {w}^{3} = - 6w$

$Det {\left(\left(A - I\right)\right)}^{2} = 36{w}^{2}$

$⇒ \alpha = 36$

questions.q: $\begin{aligned} & A(\alpha, \beta)=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}\cos \alpha & \sin \alpha & 0 \\ -\sin \alpha & \cos \alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & e^\beta\end{array}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow[A(\alpha, \beta)]^{-1}=\end{aligned}$
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \text { Given, } A(\alpha, \beta)=\left[\begin{array}{rcc}\cos \alpha & \sin \alpha & 0 \\ -\sin \alpha & \cos \alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & e^\beta\end{array}\right] \\ & \text { Now, }|A(\alpha, \beta)|=e^\beta\left(\cos ^2 \alpha+\sin ^2 \alpha\right)=e^\beta \\ & \qquad C_{11}=e^\beta \cos \alpha, C_{12}=e^\beta \sin \alpha, C_{13}=0 \\ & C_{21}=-e^\beta \sin \alpha, C_{22}=e^\beta \cos \alpha, C_{23}=0 \\ & C_{31}=0, C_{32}=0, C_{33}=\cos ^2 \alpha+\sin ^2 \alpha=1 \\ & \therefore \operatorname{adj}(A(\alpha, \beta))=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}e^\beta \cos \alpha & -e^\beta \sin \alpha & 0 \\ e^\beta \sin \alpha & -e^\beta \cos \alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right] \\ & \therefore[A(\alpha, \beta)]^{-1}=\frac{1}{e^\beta} \times e^\beta\left[\begin{array}{ccc}\cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha & 0 \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & e^{-\beta}\end{array}\right] \\ & \quad=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}\cos \alpha & -\sin \alpha & 0 \\ \sin \alpha & \cos \alpha & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & e^{-\beta}\end{array}\right]=A(-\alpha,-\beta)\end{aligned}$

A is square matrix of order `n`.

$ℓ =$ maximum number of distinct entries if `A` is a triangular matrix

$m =$ maximum number of distinct entries if `A` is a diagonal matrix

$p =$ minimum number of zeroes if `A` is a triangular matrix

If $ℓ + 5 = \text{p} + 2 \text{m}$, find the order of the matrix.
questions.solution:
$ℓ = {\text{n}}^{2} - \dfrac{\text{n} \left(\text{n} - 1\right)}{2} + 1 ​$

$\text{m} = {\text{n}}^{2} - \text{n} \left(\text{n} - 1\right) + 1$

$\text{p} = \dfrac{\text{n} \left(\text{n} - 1\right)}{2}$

Given, $ℓ + 5 = \text{p} + 2 \text{m}$

$\dfrac{{\text{n}}^{2}}{2} + \dfrac{\text{n}}{2} + 1 + 5 = \dfrac{{\text{n}}^{2}}{2} - \dfrac{\text{n}}{2} + 2 \left(\text{n} + 1\right)$

$\text{n} + 6 = 2 \text{n} + 2$

$\text{n} = 4$

questions.q: If $A$ is a non-zero square matrix of order $n$ with $\operatorname{det}(I+A) \neq 0$ and $A^3=O$, where $I, O$ are unit and null matrices of order $n \times n$ respectively, then $(I+A)^{-1}$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given, $|I+A| \neq O$
ie, $(A+I)$ is a non-singular matrix.
$O \rightarrow$ Null Matrix
$I \rightarrow$ Unit Matrix
$\because \quad I^3=I\Rightarrow \quad A^3=0\Rightarrow \quad A^3+I=O+I\Rightarrow \quad A^3+I^3=O+I\Rightarrow \quad(A+I)\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(O+I)(A+I)\left(A^2-A+I\right)=I \quad \because(O+I=I)$
Operate $(A+I)^{-1}$ on both sides
\left\{(A+I)^{-1}(A+I)\right\}\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(A+I)^{-1} \cdot I\Rightarrow \quad I \cdot\left(A^2-A+I\right)=(A+I)^{-1}  \left(\becauseI \cdot(A+I)^{-1}=(A+I)^{-1}\right)\Rightarrow \$quad(A+I)^{-1}=\left($A^2-A+I\right)$
or
$(I+A)^{-1}=  \left($I-A+A²\right)

questions.q: Let \(M\) and \(N\) be two invertible square matrices over \(R\) of order 2 such that \(N\) is diagonal. Then \(M N M^{-1}\) is diagonal ____
options: Only when \(M\) is a scalar matrix
questions.solution: Let the real matrices of order 2 \$(M=\left[\begin{array}{ll}$a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\right] $\text { and }N=\left[\begin{array}{cc}$n_1 & 0 \\ 0 & n_2 \end{array}\right]\) \(\because M\) and \(N\) are invertible matrices, so \$(M^{-1}=\frac{1}{a d-b c}\left[\begin{array}{cc}$d & -b \\ -c & a \end{array}\right]\) Therefore, \(\begin{aligned} M N M^{-1} & $=\frac{1}{a d-b c}\left[\begin{array}{ll}$a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\$right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}$n_1 & 0 \\ 0 & n_2 \end{array}\$right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}$d & -b \\ -c & a \end{array}\right] \\ & $=\frac{1}{a d-b c}\left[\begin{array}{ll}$a & b \\ c & d \end{array}\$right]\left[\begin{array}{cc}$n_1 d & -n_1 b \\ -n_2 c & n_2 a \end{array}\right] \\ & $=\frac{1}{a d-b c}\left[\begin{array}{ll}$a n_1 d-b n_2 c & -a n_1 b+b n_2 a \\ c n_1 d-d n_2 c & -c n_1 d+d n_2 a \end{array}\right] \end{aligned}\) It is given that \(M N M^{-1}\) is a diagonal matrix, then \(a $b\left($n_2-n_1\right)=0=c $d\left($n_1-n_2\right)\) and if \(M\) is a diagonal matrix, means \(b=c=0\), then the above requirement getting satisfy. Hence, option (c) is correct.$
